title: Maximum Number of Achievable Transfer Requests
summary: Given n buildings numbered 0 to n-1, each with a certain number of employees, an array of transfer requests is provided.
statement: Given n buildings numbered 0 to n-1, each with a certain number of employees, an array of transfer requests is provided. Each request is a pair [fromi, toi] indicating an employee's wish to move from building fromi to building toi. Buildings are full, so a set of requests is achievable only if the net change in employee transfers for each building is zero. Return the highest count of achievable transfer requests.
constraints: Choose the largest subset whose incoming and outgoing counts balance at every building.
hints: A chosen transfer adds one at its destination and removes one at its source.
Backtrack over include/exclude decisions while maintaining net balances.
At the leaf, accept the chosen count only when every balance is zero; prune branches unable to beat best.
Every subset corresponds to one branch path, and zero balances are exactly the feasibility condition.
editorial: Every subset corresponds to one branch path, and zero balances are exactly the feasibility condition.

tests.explanation: All three requests balance: the self-transfer changes nothing and the other two cancel.
The three-request cycle is balanced; including the extra request would unbalance buildings zero and two.
